title: Example cereal box image (teacher-made, no people)
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y4 lesson 14 (Example cereal box image (teacher-made, no people))
intro: Lesson 14: Advertising: how adverts persuade. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.h: An example cereal box (invented, no people)

passage.title: SUPER CRUNCH STARS
paras: NEW! Now with 30% MORE chocolate stars!
Packed with ENERGY for busy days!
Collect 5 tokens for a FREE toy!
Small print: per 100 g, sugars 32 g, salt 0.9 g.

questions.q: Find three persuasive techniques on the box.
questions.a: Any three: 'NEW!'; '30% MORE'; 'packed with energy' (a health-sounding claim); 'No. 1 favourite' (everyone likes it); a free toy offer; capital letters and exclamation marks.

questions.q: Who is the box aimed at, and how can you tell?
questions.a: Children: chocolate stars, a free toy, bright and exciting words.

questions.q: What does the small print tell you that the front does not?
questions.a: It is very sugary: 32 g of sugar per 100 g is high (red).

box.title: Objects and words only, no people. Use two techniques fairly (for example a true health fact and a catchy slogan).

keywords.def: a message that tries to sell something
try to make someone do or believe something
the people an advert is aimed at

questions.q: Look at the example cereal box on the slide. Name two techniques.
questions.a: Bright cartoon mascot; slogan 'Power up your morning!'

questions.q: Pupil PDF: design an HONEST advert for fruit (objects and words, no people), using two techniques fairly.
questions.a: An advert with true claims and two techniques.

questions.q: Extend: rewrite a misleading slogan to be honest.
questions.a: 'Best snack ever!' becomes 'A tasty snack for sometimes.'

questions.q: 'Collect 5 tokens for a free toy!' uses which technique?
questions.a: A) A free gift. Offers of free gifts make us buy more.

questions.q: Think again: Why do sweet adverts often use bright colours, cartoons and catchy slogans?
questions.a: To catch children's attention and make the product seem fun, so they ask for it.
